stem: The type and density of natural vegetation in a region depends primarily on:
solution: Natural vegetation is largely determined by climate — mainly temperature and moisture (rainfall).

stem: Dense tropical evergreen forests (rainforests) are found in areas with:
options: Heavy rainfall and high temperatures throughout the year
solution: Tropical evergreen (rain)forests grow in hot regions with heavy rainfall, e.g. the Amazon basin; they remain green all year.

stem: Coniferous forests, valued for softwood, are also known as:
solution: The coniferous forests of high northern latitudes are called taiga and yield softwood used for paper and furniture.

stem: The tropical grasslands of Africa are known as the:
solution: Savanna is the name for tropical grasslands, most extensively found in Africa.

stem: The temperate grasslands of North America are called the:
solution: Prairies are the temperate grasslands of North America. (Pampas = South America, Downs = Australia, Veld = South Africa.)

stem: The vegetation of the cold polar (tundra) regions consists mainly of:
solution: In the extremely cold tundra, only mosses, lichens and low shrubs can survive.

stem: Thorny bushes and scrub with long roots and thick stems are typical of which region?
solution: Thorny bushes and scrub, adapted to conserve water (long roots, waxy/thick stems), are found in hot, dry desert areas.

stem: Which of the following best explains why wildlife conservation is important?
options: Animals have no role in nature
To maintain ecological balance and protect species from extinction
To reduce the number of national parks
solution: Conserving wildlife maintains the ecological balance of nature and prevents species from becoming endangered or extinct.
